subject: Genetics
title: Beneficial Mutations
description: A micro-lesson that makes Beneficial Mutations usable.

hook.text: Most mutations are neutral. Some are harmful. A rare few give an advantage—and those are the ones evolution keeps.

buildup.text: Beneficial mutations increase fitness: better digestion, disease resistance, or environmental adaptation.

discovery.text: The EPAS1 gene variant lets Tibetans thrive at high altitude. It came from Denisovan interbreeding 40,000 years ago.

twist.text: Whether a mutation is beneficial depends entirely on environment.

climax.text: Evolution has no goal. Beneficial mutations aren't designed—they're luck that happened to match the moment.

punchline.text: Evolution doesn't plan. It just keeps what works.

quiz.question: Where did the Tibetan high-altitude gene variant come from?
